custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create an active part, part A, for this test, with 4 on hand.
    • How to do it: Click Parts in the top bar, Inventory in the left menu, then New Inventory Part. Type ZZAUTOTEST PL C425741 PART A in Description and ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C425741-A in Part Number, pick any category under Category, type 10.00 in Cost and 20.00 in Sell Price, type 4 in the Quantity of the bin row, then click Save.
  • Create an open purchase order for this test, purchase order A, with one line for another part, line 1, not yet received.
    • How to do it: Click Parts in the top bar, Purchase Orders in the left menu, then New PO; pick any Vendor, type any existing part number in Part Number and pick it, type 1 in Quantity, click Add, then Save & Close. A purchase order made this way has no work order, so its page shows the Add Order Item button.
  • Use a desktop browser that can open a second tab on the same ShopView address, signed in as the same user.
  • Start in tab 1 on purchase order A.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • A new line opens on purchase order A.

Step 2:

  • Part A is offered.

Step 3:

  • Part A fills the new line. Do not save yet.

Step 4:

  • A second tab opens.

Step 5:

  • Tab 2 shows the Parts left menu.

Step 6:

  • Tab 2 shows the Inventory page.

Step 7:

  • Part A is listed in tab 2.

Step 8:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens for part A in tab 2.

Step 9:

  • Inactive is picked.

Step 10:

  • The "Deactivate part?" confirmation opens.

Step 11:

  • Tab 2 shows "Part deactivated." and part A leaves the Active tab: part A is now inactive.

Step 12:

  • Tab 1 still shows the unsaved part A.

Step 13:

  • The save is refused with a red message: part A's part number followed by "is inactive. Activate it from the Inactive tab to use it."
  • A second, smaller line reads "Please try to resolve this."
  • Part A is not added.

Step 14:

  • The red message has gone on its own (it fades after about 3 seconds).

Step 15:

  • Line 1's part number field holds part A's number.

Step 16:

  • The change is refused with the same message, part A's part number followed by "is inactive. Activate it from the Inactive tab to use it.", and line 1 keeps its own part.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10822 (Story 9, Inactive Parts Cannot Be Added to New Work), story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog)

  • S9-R17: “The system refuses an inactive part on new work however it arrives: adding a part to a work order or estimate line, raising a part request or special order, adding a part sale line, and adding a purchase order line or changing its part or number. The refusal reads "{part number} is inactive. Activate it from the Inactive tab to use it."”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Inactive part reaches new work by another route | "{part number} is inactive. Activate it from the Inactive tab to use it." | Error toast, fades after 3 seconds”
  • Story 13, context note: “Context note: every refusal sent by the system, the rows that fade after 3 seconds, also shows a second, smaller line under the message: "Please try to resolve this." Messages the screen builds itself carry their own second line, as listed, or none.”
  • Feature Overview, Core functionality: “The system refuses an inactive part on new work however it arrives, including a part number typed by hand as a special order.”

Last checked against build v26.43.4-999c51d (QA site sv10647) on 11/3/2026.
